page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n4d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 CPU architecture and is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include any bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The CPU allocation is fully dedicated, ensuring consistent compute performance without the resource sharing typical of burstable instances. However, the provided technical specifications indicate that advanced CPU instruction sets—including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), cryptographic acceleration (AES, SHA_NI), and hardware virtualization flags—are not available on this instance. Furthermore, no benchmark performance data is currently available to evaluate its computational, memory bandwidth, or database processing capabilities.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4d-standard-4 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for standard workloads that do not require specialized hardware accelerators or local NVMe storage. The lack of bundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses represents a structural tradeoff that may require provisioning external block storage and network gateways. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, basic application hosting, and lightweight containerized microservices that fit within a 16 GB memory footprint.
